title: Solitaire
creator: Matthew Paul Argall (screenshot author, per Internet Archive item metadata)
depicted_work: Microsoft Solitaire as shipped with Microsoft Windows 95 (software copyright Microsoft Corporation)
original_date: 2024-07-28 (capture date per item metadata; host taskbar clock in the image reads 8:09 PM 28/07/2024); archive publicdate 2024-07-29 02:38:46
depicted_event_date: unknown as a period date: the image is a 2024 capture of Windows 95 software running in an Oracle VM VirtualBox virtual machine, not a 1995-era screenshot. Windows 95 release date not verified in this ticket.
acquisition_method: Anonymous public HTTP download from archive.org (no account, no terms acceptance, no gate). Checksums match the archive's own files manifest.
identity_evidence: Item metadata description: 'A screenshot I took while playing with a Windows 95 virtual machine.' File name 'Solitiare (Windows 95).png'.

In the uncropped image, the VirtualBox guest window title reads 'Windows 95 [Running] - Oracle VM VirtualBox' and the VirtualBox Manager list shows the entry 'Windows 95 / Running' with a '95' OS-type badge; the other listed VMs (Windows 3.0, 3.1, 3.11, NT 3.x, Microsoft Chicago, NT 4.0, 98, 98SE, 2000) show 'Powered Off'.

The Solitaire window inside the guest has Windows 95-style chrome: navy title bar with left app icon, and separate minimize, maximize and close (X) caption buttons. Windows 3.1 windows have no close (X) caption button, so this is not a relabelled Windows 3.1 image.
Status bar reads 'Score: 245 Time: 312'; menu bar 'Game Help'; felt colour measured as pure RGB (0,128,0), the most frequent colour in the file (164,134 pixels).

Limit: the VM name is user-assigned, and Windows NT 4.0 shares the Windows 95 shell look. The 'Running' status, the item description and the file name all point to Windows 95; the exact build (RTM/OSR) cannot be determined from the image.
original_contents_note: Uncropped Windows 11 host desktop: personal desktop icons and folder names, host taskbar with date/clock, a third-party cartoon wallpaper, File Explorer, VirtualBox Manager, and the 800x600 VirtualBox guest display (1:1 scale) showing Windows 95 with a desktop wallpaper and the Solitaire window. The original is preserved for provenance only and is not intended for on-screen use.

transformations.reversible: Yes: the untouched original is kept; the crop box, scale and offset are recorded, and src/build_editorial_frame.py reproduces the export byte-for-byte.

The removal does not change the meaning (Windows 95 Solitaire), but it also removes the in-image 'Windows 95 [Running]' label, so version identity rests on this record.
